newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Bulgaria, Macedonia edge closer with new accord.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Macedonia edge closer with new accord.

text.p: Macedonia and Bulgaria have taken a major step towards improving their often-prickly relations by signing a range of economic accords.

Bulgarian interim Prime Minsiter Stefan Sofianski said after meeting his Macedonian counterpart Branko Crvenkovski late on Thursday that he hoped their meeting would "activate contacts between neighbouring countries that have failed in the last years".
Bulgaria and Macedonia have not signed intergovernmental agreements in recent years because Skopje insists on signing any documents in both Bulgarian and Macedonian.

Bulgaria, which has complex historical relations with the former Yugoslav republic, refuses to recognise the Macedonian language, which it considers a dialect of Bulgarian. It does however recognise Macedonia as an independent state.
Thursday's agreement will strengthen economic ties and establish a free trade zone.
The two countries also plan to make a joint application to international financial institutions to get help for regional projects, in particular for building roads, railways and telephone systems.
Crvenkovski said Albania, Italy and Turkey would join the bid to financial instututions as they are involved in a plan to construct an east-west corridor.

A railway link between Sofia and Skopje has yet to be completed. It is part of a route from Turkey to the Bulgarian Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas and via Bulgaria and Macedonia to Durres in Albania.
A million-dollar east-west highway is planned to link southern Italian ports by road and rail via Albania and Macedonia with Turkey and via Bulgarian Black Sea ports with former Soviet republics.
The two Balkan countries, both struggling with the transition to a market economy, said they plan to establish a bank that will ease financial transactions between them.
